artifacts.summary: Recommends replacing check-task-references.sh's hard-coded four-tree TREE_ROOTS with a repo-wide git-ls-files scan filtered through the existing is_exempt_path (specs/** only) -- measured 0/0 equivalence against this repo's current scan; confirms the write-time hook and shared pattern lib need no changes; scopes validate-wiring.sh's independent absorbed defect (skip missing .claude/.opencode tree roots instead of hard-failing) and confirms deploy-root-guard.sh/validate-state.sh/validate-handoff-location.sh are safe; specifies two new fixture-driven test suites.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system, a repo-wide lint gate consumed by multiple downstream consumer repos of differing layout (check-task-references.sh) should default to the widest safe scope via `git ls-files` filtered through one shared exemption predicate, rather than a hard-coded list of the source-store repo's own top-level directories (TREE_ROOTS). The hard-coded-list pattern silently scans nothing relevant in a consumer repo whose layout differs, while the companion write-time hook (keyed on the file path of the current write, not an enumerated tree list) never had this problem -- a batch-scan script and a per-write hook sharing one exemption library can still diverge in effective scope if the batch scanner adds its own tree-list narrowing on top of the shared predicate.

verify-deploy.sh gate 4 (task-reference lint) only runs when $TARGET/agent-system/extensions exists, i.e. it exclusively exercises the source-store repo, never a deploy consumer -- so changes to check-task-references.sh's default scan scope are fully de-risked by measuring equivalence against the source-store repo alone; no consumer-repo CI path depends on the old four-tree behavior.
